{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox university |name = Salford Acoustics |image = Salford acoustics.jpg |image_alt = Salford Acoustics, University of Salford logo, Manchester, UK |established = 1965 |city = [[City of Salford|Salford]], [[Greater Manchester]] |country = [[England]] |type = Department, [[public university]] |motto = ''Altiora Petamus''
"Let us seek higher things" |website = http://www.acoustics.salford.ac.uk/ |campus = [[Urban area|Urban]], [[Park]]land |colours = Red, Black and White |affiliations = [[University of Salford]] }} '''Salford Acoustics''' offers [https://hub.salford.ac.uk/sirc-acoustics/acoustics-and-audio-courses/ acoustics and audio engineering courses] undertakes public and industrial [https://hub.salford.ac.uk/sirc-acoustics/ research in acoustics], carries out [https://acoustictesting.salford.ac.uk/ commercial testing] and undertakes activities to engage the public in [[Acoustics|acoustic]] science and engineering. It is based in two locations: (i) 3 km west of [[Manchester]] city centre, UK, in the [[Isaac Newton|Newton]] Building on the [[Peel Park, Salford|Peel Park]] Campus of the [[University of Salford]], and (ii) on the banks of the Manchester Ship Canal in Manchester at [[MediaCityUK]]. == History and current structure == [[File:Measuring a diffuser in an anechoic chamber.png|thumb|The second anechoic chamber at University of Salford]]The first acoustic laboratories were established in Salford in 1965; in the early 1970s the Department of Applied Acoustics was formed.{{cite journal|last=Lord|first=Peter|author2=Geoff Kerry |title=The Acoustics World|journal=Acoustics Bulletin|date=March 1997|volume=22|issue=2|pages=13}} In 1996 the university merged with University College Salford and a Department of Acoustic and Audio Engineering was formed. A couple of years later, this joined with another department to form Acoustic and Electronic Engineering. Finally, the university twice reduced the number of schools in the organisation. Salford Acoustics first joined the School of Computing, Science and Engineering and later this was merged into the School of Science, Engineering and Environment. Research work comes under the auspices of the Acoustics Research Centre. == Programmes == The Department of Applied Acoustics first taught an undergraduate degree in 1975, namely the BSc (Hons) in Electroacoustics. This was later renamed Beng (Hons) Acoustics. In 1993, Salford Acoustics set up the BEng (Hons) in Audio Technology. These two undergraduate degrees are now taught under a single banner, BEng Audio Acoustics, with two pathways to represent the different interests of the cohort.{{cite web|last=University of Salford|title=BEng Audio Acoustics|url=http://www.salford.ac.uk/ug-courses/audio-acoustics|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707185303/http://www.salford.ac.uk/ug-courses/audio-acoustics|archivedate=2013-07-07}} Salford acoustics has also taught masters in acoustic engineering and audio for many decades, currently offering an MSc in Audio Acoustics{{cite web|last=University of Salford|title=Audio Acoustics|url=http://www.salford.ac.uk/pgt-courses/audio-acoustics|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130804025834/http://www.salford.ac.uk/pgt-courses/audio-acoustics|archivedate=2013-08-04}} and an MSc in Environmental Acoustics.{{cite web|last=University of Salford|title=environmental acoustics|url=http://www.salford.ac.uk/pgt-courses/environmental-acoustics}} The Acoustics Research Centre offers masters and doctoral research degrees.{{cite web|last=University of salford|title=Phd|url=http://www.acoustics.salford.ac.uk/res/index.php?content=phd-acoustics}} == Research == === Rating === In REF2021, the feedback from the Engineering Panel (UoA12) noted, ‘outstanding impact demonstrated … live sports audio’.{{cite web|last=The University of Salford|title=REF 2021 | University of Salford |url=https://www.salford.ac.uk/research/ref-2021|accessdate=3 June 2024}} The Acoustics Research Centre achieved the top research rating of 6* in [[Research Assessment Exercise|RAE]] 2001 as part of the Research Institute for the Built and Human Environment's submission to Unit Of Assessment 30, Architecture and the Built Environment.{{cite web|last=HEFCE|title=RAE|url=http://www.rae.ac.uk/submissions/ra5a.aspx?id=30&type=uoa&subid=1384|accessdate=4 July 2013}} In 2008, the RAE submission including the Acoustics Research Centre finished top of [[Research Fortnight]]’s ‘Research Power’ table for Architecture & the Built Environment. 90% of the research was graded at international standard and 25% at world-leading.{{cite web|last=The complete University Guide|title=University of Salford|url=http://www.thecompleteuniversityguide.co.uk/salford|accessdate=4 July 2013}} === Sub-disciplines === Research is carried out in the following sub-disciplines of [[acoustical engineering|acoustic engineering]] and science * [[Archaeoacoustics]] * [[Architectural acoustics|Architectural and building acoustics]] * [[Audio signal processing]] * [[Auralization]] * Electroacoustics * [[Environmental noise]] * [[Noise control]] * Outdoor sound propagation * [[Psychoacoustics]] * [[Remote sensing]] using sound * [[Sound reproduction]] * Soundscapes * Surround sound systems * [[Vibration]] and dynamics == Public engagement == [[File:Breaking glass with sound.webm|thumb|Breaking glass with sound shot by Salford Acoustics and used in curriculum materials for schools]]Examples of public engagement work include: * The search for the Worst Sound in the World. Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council GrantRef:EP/D000068/1. * Development of extensive [https://salfordacoustics.co.uk/ curriculum materials on physics and acoustics for schools] ([[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] GrantRefs:GR/S23919/01, EP/D507030/1, P/D054729/1, EP/E033806/1, EP/G020116/1) * [http://www.sonicwonders.org/ The search for the Sonic Wonders of the World] == Laboratories == Most of Salford's Acoustics and Audio Laboratories are based on the [[Peel Park, Salford|Peel Park]] campus, but some are at [[MediaCityUK]]:{{cite web|last=University of Salford|title=Labs|url=http://www.acoustics.salford.ac.uk/facilities/}} * Audio production suites * Radio studios * Recording studios * Anechoic chamber * 2x Semi-anechoic chambers * Reverberation chamber * Transmission suite * Listening room == Commercial work == Salford Acoustics is a calibration and test house for construction, government, military, audio R&D and the motor industry.{{cite web|last=University of Salford|title=home page|url=http://www.salford.ac.uk/computing-science-engineering/subjects/acoustics-audio-and-video|accessdate=4 July 2013}} == Current staff == === Awards === {| class="wikitable" |- ! extract: Salford Acoustics offers acoustics and audio engineering courses undertakes public and industrial research in acoustics, carries out commercial testing and undertakes activities to engage the public in acoustic science and engineering. It is based in two locations: (i) 3 km west of Manchester city centre, UK, in the Newton Building on the Peel Park Campus of the University of Salford, and (ii) on the banks of the Manchester Ship Canal in Manchester at MediaCityUK.
